solution: \(P(-2\sqrt{6},\sqrt{3})\) lies on the hyperbola, so \(\frac{24}{a^{2}} - \frac{3}{b^{2}} = 1\). Also \(e = \frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}\) gives \(b^{2} = a^{2}\left(\frac{5}{4} - 1\right)\), i.e. \(a^{2} = 4b^{2}\). Then \(\frac{6}{b^{2}} - \frac{3}{b^{2}} = 1\), so \(b^{2} = 3\), \(a^{2} = 12\) and the hyperbola is \(\frac{x^{2}}{12} - \frac{y^{2}}{3} = 1\). The tangent at \(P\) is \(-\frac{x}{\sqrt{6}} - \frac{y}{\sqrt{3}} = 1\), which meets the conjugate axis \(x = 0\) at \(Q(0,-\sqrt{3})\); its slope is \(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\). The normal at \(P\) is \(y - \sqrt{3} = \sqrt{2}\left(x + 2\sqrt{6}\right)\), which meets \(x = 0\) at \(R(0,5\sqrt{3})\). Hence \(QR = 5\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{3} = 6\sqrt{3}\).
note: tangent meets the conjugate axis at (0, -sqrt3), not (0, sqrt3); only that gives QR = 6sqrt3. Key C unchanged.

solution: The tangent at \(R(3,4)\) is \(3x + 4y = 25\), so \(P\left(\frac{25}{3},0\right)\) and \(Q\left(0,\frac{25}{4}\right)\), and \(PQ = \frac{125}{12}\). Then \(OP + OQ + PQ = \frac{25}{3} + \frac{25}{4} + \frac{125}{12} = 25\). The triangle is right-angled at \(O\), so its incentre is \(\left(\frac{OP\cdot OQ}{OP + OQ + PQ}, \frac{OP\cdot OQ}{OP + OQ + PQ}\right) = \left(\frac{25}{12},\frac{25}{12}\right)\). The circle through \(O\) with this centre has \(r^{2} = 2\left(\frac{25}{12}\right)^{2} = \frac{625}{72}\).
note: wrote OP + OQ + OR = 25; the perimeter is OP + OQ + PQ = 25. Key C unchanged.

solution: \(C_{1}\) has diameter 10, passes through the origin and lies in the half-plane \(x \geq 0\), so it touches the \(y\)-axis at the origin: its centre is \((5,0)\) and \(C_{1}: x^{2} + y^{2} - 10x = 0\). With \(y = x\) this gives \(2x^{2} - 10x = 0\), so the chord runs from the origin \((0,0)\) to \((5,5)\). \(C_2\) has this as diameter, so its centre is the midpoint \(O_2=(\tfrac52,\tfrac52)\). The chord of \(C_2\) through \((2,3)\) farthest from \(O_2\) is perpendicular to \(O_2(2,3)\); that segment has slope \(\frac{3-2.5}{2-2.5}=-1\), so the chord has slope \(1\): \(y-3=(x-2)\Rightarrow x-y+1=0\). Thus \(a=-1,\;b=1\) and \(a-b=-2\).
note: the endpoint (5, 5) was asserted; added why: C1 lies in x >= 0 through O, so its centre is (5, 0). Key C unchanged.

solution: The tangent at \(P(2,-4)\) to \(y^{2} = 8x\) is \(-4y = 4(x + 2)\), i.e. \(x + y + 2 = 0\). The normal at \(P\) is perpendicular to it: \(x - y + \lambda = 0\) through \((2,-4)\) gives \(\lambda = -6\), i.e. \(x - y = 6\). The directrix is \(x = -2\): the tangent meets it at \(A(-2,0)\) and the normal at \(B(-2,-8)\). For \(AQBP\) to be a square, \(Q = A + B - P = (-6,-4)\), so \(a = -6\), \(b = -4\) and \(2a + b = -16\).
note: B was written A(-2, 8); the normal meets the directrix at B(-2, -8). Rewritten cleanly. Key A unchanged.

solution: Take \(P(1 + \cos\theta, 1 + \sin\theta)\) on the circle. Then \(PA^{2} = \cos^{2}\theta + (\sin\theta - 3)^{2} = 10 - 6\sin\theta\) and \(PB^{2} = \cos^{2}\theta + (\sin\theta + 6)^{2} = 37 + 12\sin\theta\), so \(PA^{2} + PB^{2} = 47 + 6\sin\theta\), which is greatest at \(\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}\), i.e. \(P(1,2)\). Then \(P\), \(A\) and \(B\) all lie on the line \(x = 1\).
note: PB^2 sign error (wrote 37 - 12 sin); it is 37 + 12 sin, so the maximum is at pi/2 (P(1,2)), not 3pi/2. Still collinear on x = 1; key B unchanged.

solution: For \(y^2=-\tfrac{x}{2}\), a line \(y=m(x-2)\) through \((2,0)\) gives \(m^{2}x^{2} + \left(\tfrac12 - 4m^{2}\right)x + 4m^{2} = 0\), and it is tangent when the discriminant vanishes: \(\tfrac14-4m^2=0\Rightarrow m=\pm\tfrac14\). The tangents are \(x\mp4y-2=0\); the distance from \((5,0)\) equals the circle radius \(\sqrt r=\frac{|5-2|}{\sqrt{17}}=\frac{3}{\sqrt{17}}\). Hence \(r=\tfrac{9}{17}\) and \(17r=9\).
note: discriminant written -4m^2 + 1/2 = 0 (gives m^2 = 1/8); it is 1/4 - 4m^2 = 0, m = +-1/4. Answer 9 unchanged.

solution: \((4,4\sqrt{3})\) lies on \(y^{2} = 4ax\), so \(48 = 16a\), \(4a = 12\) and the parabola is \(y^{2} = 12x\). The parameter of \(P\) is \(t_{1} = \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\), so for the focal chord \(t_{2} = -\frac{1}{t_1} = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) and \(Q\left(\frac{9}{4}, -3\sqrt{3}\right)\). The area of trapezium \(PQNM\) is \(\frac{1}{2}MN\cdot(PM + QN) = \frac{1}{2}MN\cdot(PS + QS) = \frac{1}{2}MN\cdot PQ = \frac{1}{2}\cdot 7\sqrt{3}\cdot\frac{49}{4} = \frac{343\sqrt{3}}{8}\).
note: a stray '= 3' ended the final line; removed. Key C unchanged.

solution: From the circle, \(y^{2} = 8x - x^{2}\); the hyperbola is \(4x^{2} - 9y^{2} = 36\). Substituting, \(4x^{2} - 9(8x - x^{2}) = 36\), i.e. \(13x^{2} - 72x - 36 = 0\), so \((13x + 6)(x - 6) = 0\). For \(x = -\frac{6}{13}\), \(y^{2} < 0\), so it is rejected; \(x = 6\) gives \(y^{2} = 12\). So \(A(6,\sqrt{12})\) and \(B(6,-\sqrt{12})\). Let \(P\left(\alpha,\frac{2\alpha + 4}{3}\right)\) on the line and \((h,k)\) the centroid: \(h = \frac{12 + \alpha}{3}\), so \(\alpha = 3h - 12\), and \(k = \frac{2\alpha + 4}{9}\), so \(\alpha = \frac{9k - 4}{2}\). Equating, \(6h - 24 = 9k - 4\), i.e. \(6h - 9k = 20\): the centroid lies on \(6x - 9y = 20\).
note: '6h - 2y = 9k - 4' should be 6h - 24 = 9k - 4; also cleaned garbled lines ((x = 6), y = I sqrt12, 2x - 3y + y = 0). Key D unchanged.

solution: The line joining the centres is perpendicular to the common tangent \(4x + 3y = 10\) (slope \(-\frac{4}{3}\)), so its slope is \(\frac{3}{4} = \tan\theta\), with \(\cos\theta = \frac{4}{5}\), \(\sin\theta = \frac{3}{5}\). The centres are 5 from \((1,2)\) along it: \((1 \pm 5\cos\theta, 2 \pm 5\sin\theta)\), i.e. \(C_{1}(5,5)\) and \(C_{2}(-3,-1)\). Hence \(|(\alpha + \beta)(\gamma + \delta)| = |10 \times (-4)| = 40\).
note: the line of centres was given slope 4/3; it is perpendicular to the tangent, slope 3/4, so the centres are (5,5) and (-3,-1), not (4,6) and (-2,-2) (the 40 was a coincidence). Answer 40 unchanged.

solution: The normal to \(y^{2} = 8x\) is \(y = mx - 4m - 2m^{3}\). The shortest distance runs along the normal through the circle's centre \((0,-6)\): \(-6 = -4m - 2m^{3}\), i.e. \(m^{3} + 2m - 3 = 0\), so \((m - 1)(m^{2} + m + 3) = 0\) and \(m = 1\). Then \(P = (am^{2}, -2am) = (2,-4)\). The circle has centre \(C(0,-6)\) and radius 1, and \(PC = \sqrt{4 + 4} = 2\sqrt{2}\), so the shortest distance is \(PC - r = 2\sqrt{2} - 1\).
note: said m = -1; the factorisation gives m = 1 (P(2, -4) is for m = 1). Key D unchanged.
e^2 was written (1 - b^2)/a^2 (it is 1 - b^2/a^2) with garbled steps after it; rewritten. Key B unchanged.

solution: Equation of circle is \[(x + 3)(x - \alpha) + (y - 2)(y - 4) = 0\] \(Q\) lies on it \[12(9 - \alpha) + 8 \times 6 = 0\] \[\alpha = 13\] \[x^{2} + y^{2} - 10x - 6y - 31 = 0\] Equation of Tangent at \(Q\) \[x.9 + y.10 - 5(x + 9) - 3(y + 10) - 31 = 0\] \[4x + 7y = 106\] Equation of Tangent at \(R\) \[x.13 + y.4 - 5(x + 13) - 3(y + 4) - 31 = 0\] \[8x + y = 108\] Solution (a) and (b) \[s = \left( \frac{25}{2},8 \right)\] which lies on \(2x - ky = 1\) \[k = 3\]

solution: Centre of the circle \(= \left( \frac{3}{2},1 \right)\), and \(AB\) is a diameter, so the centre lies on \(2x + 3y - k = 0\): \[2\left( \frac{3}{2} \right) + 3(1) - k = 0\] \[\Rightarrow k = 6\] Now, Equation of ellipse becomes \[x^{2} + 9y^{2} = 36\] \[\frac{x^{2}}{6^{2}} + \frac{y^{2}}{2^{2}} = 1 \]length of \(LR = \frac{2b^{2}}{a} = \frac{2 \cdot 2^{2}}{6} = \frac{8}{6} = \frac{4}{3} = \frac{m}{n}\) \[\therefore 2\text{ }m + n = 2(4) + 3 = 11\]

solution: \[\frac{x^{2}}{9} - \frac{y^{2}}{4} = 1\] \[a^{2} = 9,b^{2} = 4\] \[b^{2} = a^{2}\left( e^{2} - 1 \right) \Rightarrow e^{2} = 1 + \frac{b^{2}}{a^{2}}\] \[e^{2} = 1 + \frac{4}{9} = \frac{13}{9}\] \[e = \frac{\sqrt{13}}{3} \Rightarrow S_{1}S_{2} = 2ae = 2 \times 3 \times \frac{\sqrt{13}}{3} = 2\sqrt{13}\] Area of \(\Delta{PS}_{1}{\text{ }S}_{2} = \frac{1}{2} \times \beta \times S_{1}{\text{ }S}_{2} = 2\sqrt{13}\) \[\Rightarrow \frac{1}{2} \times \beta \times (2\sqrt{13}) = 2\sqrt{13} \Rightarrow \beta = 2\] \[\frac{\alpha^{2}}{9} - \frac{\beta^{2}}{4} = 1 \Rightarrow \frac{\alpha^{2}}{9} - 1 = 1 \Rightarrow \alpha^{2} = 18 \Rightarrow \alpha = 3\sqrt{2}\] Distance of \(P\) from origin \(= \sqrt{\alpha^{2} + \beta^{2}}\) \[= \sqrt{18 + 4} = \sqrt{22}\]
note: 2ae was written 2 x 3 x sqrt(13/3); it is 2 x 3 x sqrt13/3 = 2 sqrt13. Key C unchanged.
